ZCG’s 8% funding stream ends when this ZIP activates. For the rest of that stream’s term, the same 8% of the block subsidy goes into a new lockbox, the
Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox
, which holds it for future Zcash development and legal defense.

The ZCG Committee removes 50,000 ZEC from circulation, crediting it to the NSM, using ZIP 233’s removal mechanism if it is available when this ZIP activates. An unspendable address is specified only as a last resort: it is used, and given consensus and wallet treatment under this ZIP, only if ZIP 233 is not available.

The rapid rise in the price of ZEC has enlarged the monetary value of ZCG’s treasury to a much greater amount than ever before. This ZIP reduces the risks and pressure that come with large amounts of money, removes ZCG funds from circulation, crediting the Network Sustainability Mechanism (providing increased long-term issuance), and accrues funds in a lockbox for future use by the Zcash community.

The Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox

The Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox is a second lockbox, separate from the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox, with its own chain value pool balance. It holds funds for future Zcash development and legal defense. No disbursement mechanism is currently defined for this lockbox; the Zcash community will need to decide upon and specify a suitable decentralized mechanism for permitting withdrawals from this lockbox in a future ZIP in order to make these funds available for funding Zcash development and legal defense.

The section “The removal of ZCG funds” requires the ZCG Committee to remove 50,000 ZEC from circulation, crediting it to the NSM. The intended means is ZIP 233
, which lets a sender voluntarily remove a specified amount of ZEC from circulation; ZIP 237 credits removed value to the NSM Value Balance

Unless the fallback is explicitly selected, the address MUST NOT be used to fulfill this ZIP’s removal obligation, and implementations MUST NOT give the address or its script any special consensus accounting or wallet recognition under this ZIP. In particular, payments to it MUST NOT be credited to the NSM Value Balance. The absence of ZIP 233 alone does not select the fallback.
Where ZIP 233 is selected, its own consensus rules perform the removal: a v7 transaction
, which is removed from circulation when the transaction is mined, and which ZIP 237 adds to the NSM Value Balance. On such a network, this ZIP adds no consensus rules.

The NSM removal address looks like any other Mainnet P2SH address; nothing about it warns a user that funds sent to it cannot be recovered. Software that accepts payment destinations — typed or pasted by a user, read from a payment request URI, or kept in an address book — SHOULD recognize the NSM removal address, by its script hash or its exact string, at every such entry point; SHOULD present a payment to it as an irreversible removal of funds from circulation, not an ordinary payment; and SHOULD NOT offer it as an ordinary payment destination.

The ZCG Committee SHALL cause 50,000 ZEC of the funds it administers to be removed from circulation, crediting it to the NSM, in one or more Mainnet transactions using the mechanism selected by the deployment ZIP. The specified removal amounts MUST total that amount, excluding transaction fees. If the address fallback is selected, these are the amounts paid to that address. The 8% is set aside, issued but locked, for future development and legal defense, and a future ZIP decides how it is spent. A separate balance keeps the fund apart from the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox’s purpose and disbursement rules, and lets a future disbursement mechanism authorize withdrawals from each lockbox separately — under ZIP 270’s tracked signing keys

, for example, each can have authorizing keys of its own. Like that lockbox, it needs no custodians or keys today, and its disbursement mechanism can take the same technical approach as the one being designed for the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox.
An address only as a last resort.
ZIP 233 is the protocol’s purpose-built way to remove funds from circulation: an explicit amount in a v7 transaction, with no address. NU7 deploys neither ZIP 233 nor ZIP 248’s v7 format

, and this ZIP cannot anticipate whether they will be available when it activates, so it reserves the address solely for the case where they are not. If needed, the fallback requires no new transaction fields or address formats, recognizes only one script, and is permanent, so value sent to the address at any height is added to the NSM Value Balance; if ZIP 233 activates later, both mechanisms add to the same balance.
Spending from the NSM removal address would require a redeem script other than

with the same script hash — a preimage attack on RIPEMD-160. This ZIP adds no rule against such a spend: an attack of that kind would threaten the much larger value held in ordinary transparent outputs, and a rule for this one address would not change that.
50,000 ZEC is about 55% of ZCG’s ZEC. Anyone can check the removal on the chain, and ZCG keeps the rest of its treasury and its grants program.

The lockbox’s balance stays in the Issued Supply. A ZIP 233 removal subtracts its amount from the Issued Supply when its transaction is mined; where the fallback is selected, a payment to the NSM removal address leaves the transparent pool at the height ZIP 237 credits it. In each case, the value moves to the NSM Value Balance in the same block, keeping ZIP 237’s invariant: in each block from NU7 on, the Issued Supply plus the NSM Value Balance grows by exactly the scheduled block subsidy.
ZIP draft #1414 sends the 8% stream to the NSM
. Where they overlap with this ZIP, they are alternatives to it.
The lockbox rules — and, if the fallback is selected, the NSM removal address rules — are consensus changes, proposed for a network upgrade after NU7 that activates before height

. The removal of ZCG funds follows the schedule in the section “The removal of ZCG funds”.
